name: Mitigation

subjectOf.text: Hedge funds have the potential both to amplify and to mitigate systemic risk, and which effect dominates turns on their particular risk management incentives, leverage, and investment strategies, which is why the academic evidence remains mixed.
subjectOf.abstract: Hedge funds may have the potential to amplify and/or mitigate systemic risks due to their particular risk management incentives, leverage, and investment strategies.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Timothy A. Krause, Hedge Funds and Systemic Risk (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2748096
scope_conditions: conclusion drawn from the mixed post-crisis literature

subjectOf.text: The incentives that undermine long term success of the hybrid model can be mitigated by mandating that staking on deals requires capital commitments, while allowing VCs to lower their capital commitments and increase their staking over time.
subjectOf.abstract: It is possible to mitigate these incentives that undermine the long-term success of the system. For example, it is conceivable that staking on deals by VCs mandates capital commitments to the deals but that VCs can over time lower their capital commitments and increase their staking.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, REPUTATION AS CAPITAL – How Decentralized Autonomous Organizations Address Shortcomings in the Ventu (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3962614
scope_conditions: hybrid VC DAO models transitioning away from capital
